title: Chocolate Tres Leches Cake
changes_from_base: 40 g cocoa replaces 40 g flour in the sponge, and cocoa and dark chocolate are melted into the three milks.
summary: A chocolate version of the classic tres leches cake, following the same soaking method but with cocoa worked into the sponge and melted into the milk soak for a deeper flavour.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm metal baking tin (at least 5 cm deep)
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the tin and oven
steps.text: This follows the classic tres leches method, with cocoa worked into both the sponge and the milk soak for a deeper chocolate flavour. Set the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) and give it a good 20 minutes to come up to heat, with a rack placed centrally. Grease only the base of the tin, leaving the sides bare so the sponge has something to grip as it rises.

steps.title: Whisk the eggs
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt on high speed for 6-8 minutes until tripled in volume and thick. Whisk in the vanilla, and warm the milk gently alongside, ready for folding in.

steps.title: Fold in flour and cocoa
steps.text: Sift the flour, cocoa powder and baking powder over the whisked eggs in two additions, folding in gently, then fold in the warm milk. Pour into the tin and bake for 25-30 minutes until springy to the touch. Folding gently protects the air whisked into the eggs, which gives the sponge its only lift.

steps.title: Soak with chocolate milk
steps.text: Let the cocoa-rich sponge rest for 20 minutes, then pierce it evenly across the surface with a skewer, spacing each hole 1-2 cm apart. Heat the evaporated milk, condensed milk, whole milk and cocoa together in a saucepan until steaming, stir in the chopped dark chocolate until melted, then cool to warm. Pour the chocolate milk slowly over the cake in 3-4 additions, letting each soak in before adding the next; melting the chocolate straight into the warm milk spreads its flavour evenly through every soak.

steps.title: Chill to soak through
steps.text: Cover the cake and chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, so the chocolate milk has time to work all the way through the sponge rather than sitting near the surface.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Whip the double cream with the icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks and spread over the cold, soaked cake. Dust with cocoa powder and top each portion with a strawberry. Cut into 12 squares and serve cold, with the chocolate milk pooling around each slice.

tips: Grease only the base of the tin, not the sides, so the sponge has something to grip as it rises.
Melt the chocolate into the warm milk mixture, not straight onto the cake, so it spreads evenly instead of setting in solid patches.
Prick the sponge evenly before soaking, or the chocolate milk will pool rather than soak through.
Pour the milk in stages and let each one absorb - pouring it all in one go causes a soggy base and dry top.
Chill overnight if you can; a shorter rest leaves the centre drier than the edges.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the cake covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days; it is not suitable for freezing once soaked. Serve chilled, straight from the fridge.
